content:
marie: Hey team — I opened a small PR to reconcile the SDK snippets for function/tool calling and the structured output section. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1798
ajay: thanks — saw that. main issue is the JS snippet still uses the old `callTool()` shape, which our runtime no longer emits.
samira: can you paste the problematic snippet here? I can patch the TS one quickly. :+1:
marie: sure — in the PR the JS example has:
```js
const result = await client.callTool('calculator', { expression: '12*7' })
console.log(result.output)
```
but the current SDK returns a structured envelope: `{ data: { result: ... }, meta: { tool: 'calculator' } }`
bobby: yep — runtime now returns the envelope to support tool provenance. docs need to show both the compact parse and the envelope unwrap pattern. otherwise folks will be confused when `result.output` is undefined.
luis: also noticed a broken internal link in the same page: docs/guides/structured-output.md -> examples/math.md (404). I filed a quick link fix in the PR comments.
marie: plan I propose: 1) replace old snippet with unified pattern that shows both: the canonical envelope, then a helper `unwrapTool()` helper snippet; 2) add a note about parse fallback for older runtime responses; 3) fix link and add a test reference.
ajay: that sounds good. for the helper, let's keep it tiny and language-idiomatic. e.g.:
```js
function unwrapTool(resp) {
  return resp?.data?.result ?? resp?.output ?? null
}
```
samira: I can add a TS helper and an example using `as const` for typed parse. I'll also drop a tiny Python one-liner for quickstarts.
bobby: one quick concern — regen examples for `function-calling.md` because we changed the schema keys from `tool_output` -> `data.result`. We should run the sample LLM outputs through the parser tests. I can trigger the `samples/regenerate` job.
marie: great. @docs-bot can you add labels `docs:snippets` and `needs:link-fix` to the PR?
docs-bot: labels added: docs:snippets, needs:link-fix (automated)
samira: FYI I found a small edge case where the schema has nullable arrays — will add a short paragraph about array canonicalization and include this sample parse pattern:
```js
// prefer array of items, but accept null -> []
const items = Array.isArray(resp.data.items) ? resp.data.items : (resp.data.items == null ? [] : [resp.data.items])
```
luis: love that. can we also add a one-line callout about canary rollouts? a note that some Hosted customers may see legacy shapes during rollout for a day. avoids confusion.
ajay: add this as a small caution block. Ops already warned about a handful of customers on the old runtime.
marie: timeline: I can push edits this afternoon. @bobby if you kick the regen job, drop a short ok or fail in the PR comments. samira — can you handle the TS + Python snippets? luis — can you add the canary callout copy?
bobby: will run regen now, linking logs in the PR.
docs-bot: regen job started: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/jobs/98765
bobby: regen finished — one sample mismatch, updated in branch `marie/docs-snippet-fix`. details in the job log.
samira: pushed TS + python helpers and added types example. Also fixed the broken link to examples/math.md.
marie: I updated the page with the unified snippet and the fallback paragraph. also added a tiny test-case in `docs/tests/parse_examples.test.js` to assert `unwrapTool` behavior.
luis: copy looks good; I shortened the canary note.
ajay: quick review request submitted. :eyes:
marie: thanks — assigning to @ajay and @bobby for final tech check. once approved I'll merge and backfill the changelog entry. :tada:
